Keep every row in order. Preserve all [[I]], [[B]], [[SC]] emphasis markers, [[Nnumber]] note markers and explicit source line counts. Do not return hashes; the host binds immutable hashes.", "context": {"title": "David Copperfield", "unit": 50, "heading": "CHAPTER 48. DOMESTIC", "previous_rows": [], "source_language": "English", "part": null, "book": null, "chapter": 48, "role": "chapter"}, "source_rows": [{"id": "en85-u050-h", "tag": "h2", "role": "heading", "text": "CHAPTER 48. DOMESTIC", "sha256": "b322667de30b9892408d1d97dec88d7946e177e7eccfd0aa3574dce9b60cec25", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[55]/h2", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": []}, {"id": "en85-u050-b0001", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I laboured hard at my book, without allowing it to interfere with the punctual discharge of my newspaper duties; and it came out and was very successful. I was not stunned by the praise which sounded in my ears, notwithstanding that I was keenly alive to it, and thought better of my own performance, I have little doubt, than anybody else did. It has always been in my observation of human nature, that a man who has any good reason to believe in himself never flourishes himself before the faces of other people in order that they may believe in him. For this reason, I retained my modesty in very self-respect; and the more praise I got, the more I tried to deserve.", "sha256": "2ee8ad2e58701e150d4fee2e5c2efcf50649c77cc3838e4397cb09d429ecc206", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[55]/p[1]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u050-b0002", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "It is not my purpose, in this record, though in all other essentials it is my written memory, to pursue the history of my own fictions. They express themselves, and I leave them to themselves. When I refer to them, incidentally, it is only as a part of my progress.", "sha256": "4da356045e22a3eb727cf3ed95ff52112aea62b887a58a5aacddc5aaab3033e7", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[55]/p[2]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u050-b0003", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Having some foundation for believing, by this time, that nature and accident had made me an author, I pursued my vocation with confidence. Without such assurance I should certainly have left it alone, and bestowed my energy on some other endeavour. I should have tried to find out what nature and accident really had made me, and to be that, and nothing else. I had been writing, in the newspaper and elsewhere, so prosperously, that when my new success was achieved, I considered myself reasonably entitled to escape from the dreary debates. One joyful night, therefore, I noted down the music of the parliamentary bagpipes for the last time, and I have never heard it since; though I still recognize the old drone in the newspapers, without any substantial variation (except, perhaps, that there is more of it), all the livelong session.", "sha256": "edb374054aafc779c22b7434cac0618f31805e73318ffcc15db6de7a774e2efb", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[55]/p[3]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u050-b0004", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I now write of the time when I had been married, I suppose, about a year and a half. After several varieties of experiment, we had given up the housekeeping as a bad job. The house kept itself, and we kept a page. The principal function of this retainer was to quarrel with the cook; in which respect he was a perfect Whittington, without his cat, or the remotest chance of being made Lord Mayor.", "sha256": "3b50f869cfddd274521ee34dc5462c4047314277b029ac01265c999b678f29a8", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[55]/p[4]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u050-b0005", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "He appears to me to have lived in a hail of saucepan-lids. His whole existence was a scuffle. He would shriek for help on the most improper occasions,—as when we had a little dinner-party, or a few friends in the evening,—and would come tumbling out of the kitchen, with iron missiles flying after him. We wanted to get rid of him, but he was very much attached to us, and wouldn’t go. He was a tearful boy, and broke into such deplorable lamentations, when a cessation of our connexion was hinted at, that we were obliged to keep him. He had no mother—no anything in the way of a relative, that I could discover, except a sister, who fled to America the moment we had taken him off her hands; and he became quartered on us like a horrible young changeling. He had a lively perception of his own unfortunate state, and was always rubbing his eyes with the sleeve of his jacket, or stooping to blow his nose on the extreme corner of a little pocket-handkerchief, which he never would take completely out of his pocket, but always economized and secreted.", "sha256": "4a9aa617411e6a4145b93287d27d4b427015b15770f87b0adc5486336dc3705f", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[55]/p[5]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u050-b0006", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "This unlucky page, engaged in an evil hour at six pounds ten per annum, was a source of continual trouble to me. I watched him as he grew—and he grew like scarlet beans—with painful apprehensions of the time when he would begin to shave; even of the days when he would be bald or grey. I saw no prospect of ever getting rid of him; and, projecting myself into the future, used to think what an inconvenience he would be when he was an old man.", "sha256": "4c77eaec7e98db99c7a59830488988736f7e0bb0bc5748849b48675945891dd5", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[55]/p[6]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u050-b0007", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I never expected anything less, than this unfortunate’s manner of getting me out of my difficulty. He stole Dora’s watch, which, like everything else belonging to us, had no particular place of its own; and, converting it into money, spent the produce (he was always a weak-minded boy) in incessantly riding up and down between London and Uxbridge outside the coach. He was taken to Bow Street, as well as I remember, on the completion of his fifteenth journey; when four-and-sixpence, and a second-hand fife which he couldn’t play, were found upon his person.", "sha256": "256687602ef73dc374d56fcf10efc17067703e10259bd07d51a8cfa73adfe3b9", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[55]/p[7]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u050-b0008", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "The surprise and its consequences would have been much less disagreeable to me if he had not been penitent. But he was very penitent indeed, and in a peculiar way—not in the lump, but by instalments. For example: the day after that on which I was obliged to appear against him, he made certain revelations touching a hamper in the cellar, which we believed to be full of wine, but which had nothing in it except bottles and corks. We supposed he had now eased his mind, and told the worst he knew of the cook; but, a day or two afterwards, his conscience sustained a new twinge, and he disclosed how she had a little girl, who, early every morning, took away our bread; and also how he himself had been suborned to maintain the milkman in coals. In two or three days more, I was informed by the authorities of his having led to the discovery of sirloins of beef among the kitchen-stuff, and sheets in the rag-bag. A little while afterwards, he broke out in an entirely new direction, and confessed to a knowledge of burglarious intentions as to our premises, on the part of the pot-boy, who was immediately taken up. I got to be so ashamed of being such a victim, that I would have given him any money to hold his tongue, or would have offered a round bribe for his being permitted to run away. It was an aggravating circumstance in the case that he had no idea of this, but conceived that he was making me amends in every new discovery: not to say, heaping obligations on my head.", "sha256": "e27a0a0bb540442662ba4106afeb959334a7fb09ad6e0377df00ae5f33499ab2", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[55]/p[8]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u050-b0009", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "At last I ran away myself, whenever I saw an emissary of the police approaching with some new intelligence; and lived a stealthy life until he was tried and ordered to be transported. Even then he couldn’t be quiet, but was always writing us letters; and wanted so much to see Dora before he went away, that Dora went to visit him, and fainted when she found herself inside the iron bars. In short, I had no peace of my life until he was expatriated, and made (as I afterwards heard) a shepherd of, ‘up the country’ somewhere; I have no geographical idea where.", "sha256": "ecab612f46389d7c9ef59e27b6669b066140bb2dc436590868b35b17f9bafedc", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[55]/p[9]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u050-b0010", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "All this led me into some serious reflections, and presented our mistakes in a new aspect; as I could not help communicating to Dora one evening, in spite of my tenderness for her.", "sha256": "267ce31f05df0147bc6483ee22310410ef7213d7b4e60b7305ea98f0ba3cc64f", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[55]/p[10]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u050-b0011", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘My love,’ said I, ‘it is very painful to me to think that our want of system and management, involves not only ourselves (which we have got used to), but other people.’", "sha256": "4f7d28528057276b15f7da85d4523e185a148c23f52b230349cf11fa200d89f8", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[55]/p[11]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u050-b0012", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘You have been silent for a long time, and now you are going to be cross!’ said Dora.", "sha256": "a014cd20c435d1dca4d0bc9dfcfb964ff103e2eaa3e539e9148312135cc4671b", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[55]/p[12]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u050-b0013", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘No, my dear, indeed! Let me explain to you what I mean.’", "sha256": "0fd6ff8bec90aa38ef22ead8705539988a3f3ef4ce70b585e3e742f1c9c53476", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[55]/p[13]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u050-b0014", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I think I don’t want to know,’ said Dora.", "sha256": "7ce0e83d6c3be3c4c08ed1e50ba52ca9ccc74149b24a71658c876478cdf5316c", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[55]/p[14]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u050-b0015", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘But I want you to know, my love. Put Jip down.’", "sha256": "675f5c13913c9be5becd80bf9dc0a5129a4a7a5443511efeb3cafbcb0ff5afcc", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[55]/p[15]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u050-b0016", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Dora put his nose to mine, and said ‘Boh!’ to drive my seriousness away; but, not succeeding, ordered him into his Pagoda, and sat looking at me, with her hands folded, and a most resigned little expression of countenance.", "sha256": "2665bd294dc48716e22726eb22f2bfc919b7e4f84585e129cd31bf6529771dea", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[55]/p[16]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u050-b0017", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘The fact is, my dear,’ I began, ‘there is contagion in us. We infect everyone about us.’", "sha256": "3ab557b6b9545e28b5c95486fa5c084a76dc4ec36f6396b4e779d23fcf6ec5a4", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[55]/p[17]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u050-b0018", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I might have gone on in this figurative manner, if Dora’s face had not admonished me that she was wondering with all her might whether I was going to propose any new kind of vaccination, or other medical remedy, for this unwholesome state of ours. Therefore I checked myself, and made my meaning plainer.", "sha256": "52478f817bd3c0e164877bf986c6101306c0c35f2b147200d0807c15dd4cbf0b", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[55]/p[18]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u050-b0019", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘It is not merely, my pet,’ said I, ‘that we lose money and comfort, and even temper sometimes, by not learning to be more careful; but that we incur the serious responsibility of spoiling everyone who comes into our service, or has any dealings with us. I begin to be afraid that the fault is not entirely on one side, but that these people all turn out ill because we don’t turn out very well ourselves.’", "sha256": "948eb7924a4980f49c29da63eb0e2c7767af7255023bf343089e61be37182f85", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[55]/p[19]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u050-b0020", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Oh, what an accusation,’ exclaimed Dora, opening her eyes wide; ‘to say that you ever saw me take gold watches! Oh!’", "sha256": "16c8352c046b3726ac3d08b61ac44227eb1c668366064512f4eb49a49548e8d7", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[55]/p[20]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u050-b0021", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘My dearest,’ I remonstrated, ‘don’t talk preposterous nonsense! Who has made the least allusion to gold watches?’", "sha256": "6da4b6bb8b9e3a820bc35cce9458315d991feb5aec5e6ed0a3df29992c01bd19", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[55]/p[21]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u050-b0022", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘You did,’ returned Dora. ‘You know you did. You said I hadn’t turned out well, and compared me to him.’", "sha256": "b3f563b170d6bc81204280463d5654557979e5b0644d9e15e6d68df10243792e", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[55]/p[22]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u050-b0023", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘To whom?’ I asked.", "sha256": "b956667df47f9c43f91b918a6679e9502c0a5ec861b800a261ee0dcfa935418b", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[55]/p[23]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u050-b0024", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘To the page,’ sobbed Dora. ‘Oh, you cruel fellow, to compare your affectionate wife to a transported page! Why didn’t you tell me your opinion of me before we were married? Why didn’t you say, you hard-hearted thing, that you were convinced I was worse than a transported page? Oh, what a dreadful opinion to have of me! Oh, my goodness!’", "sha256": "62316016fa3213a23d756c44f7db83cc7a77e8d5ad6c44da41addc85e1d687ee", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[55]/p[24]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u050-b0025", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Now, Dora, my love,’ I returned, gently trying to remove the handkerchief she pressed to her eyes, ‘this is not only very ridiculous of you, but very wrong. In the first place, it’s not true.’", "sha256": "ddda34a82f8f1bba29dcb3bcbb2d3e8468b85f41dfe84a6530b44eb3cfe85403", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[55]/p[25]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u050-b0026", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘You always said he was a story-teller,’ sobbed Dora. ‘And now you say the same of me! Oh, what shall I do! What shall I do!’", "sha256": "99ef223abcb9ac0afce214a80580d696d43f024736100371e843725e4e13b6df", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[55]/p[26]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u050-b0027", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘My darling girl,’ I retorted, ‘I really must entreat you to be reasonable, and listen to what I did say, and do say. My dear Dora, unless we learn to do our duty to those whom we employ, they will never learn to do their duty to us. I am afraid we present opportunities to people to do wrong, that never ought to be presented. Even if we were as lax as we are, in all our arrangements, by choice—which we are not—even if we liked it, and found it agreeable to be so—which we don’t—I am persuaded we should have no right to go on in this way. We are positively corrupting people. We are bound to think of that. I can’t help thinking of it, Dora. It is a reflection I am unable to dismiss, and it sometimes makes me very uneasy. There, dear, that’s all. Come now. Don’t be foolish!’", "sha256": "4b078bd05022bec05451a9e91f390411e88752254d372ca1555fa6429de3c837", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[55]/p[27]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u050-b0028", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Dora would not allow me, for a long time, to remove the handkerchief. She sat sobbing and murmuring behind it, that, if I was uneasy, why had I ever been married? Why hadn’t I said, even the day before we went to church, that I knew I should be uneasy, and I would rather not? If I couldn’t bear her, why didn’t I send her away to her aunts at Putney, or to Julia Mills in India? Julia would be glad to see her, and would not call her a transported page; Julia never had called her anything of the sort. In short, Dora was so afflicted, and so afflicted me by being in that condition, that I felt it was of no use repeating this kind of effort, though never so mildly, and I must take some other course.", "sha256": "a29d3d3c0c201c491b8e591527ce30a258a318191c9b35b40be0e29d463f7b1a", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[55]/p[28]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u050-b0029", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "What other course was left to take? To ‘form her mind’? This was a common phrase of words which had a fair and promising sound, and I resolved to form Dora’s mind.", "sha256": "9790179df646c422212c54e9d4cfb0cb98805913b6cfd206842729317ef14b56", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[55]/p[29]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u050-b0030", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I began immediately. When Dora was very childish, and I would have infinitely preferred to humour her, I tried to be grave—and disconcerted her, and myself too. I talked to her on the subjects which occupied my thoughts; and I read Shakespeare to her—and fatigued her to the last degree. I accustomed myself to giving her, as it were quite casually, little scraps of useful information, or sound opinion—and she started from them when I let them off, as if they had been crackers. No matter how incidentally or naturally I endeavoured to form my little wife’s mind, I could not help seeing that she always had an instinctive perception of what I was about, and became a prey to the keenest apprehensions. In particular, it was clear to me, that she thought Shakespeare a terrible fellow. The formation went on very slowly.", "sha256": "9b159615b5cceef93ed32d7af4a772118b559564e2a79a4a652173763e458dfb", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[55]/p[30]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u050-b0031", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I pressed Traddles into the service without his knowledge; and whenever he came to see us, exploded my mines upon him for the edification of Dora at second hand. The amount of practical wisdom I bestowed upon Traddles in this manner was immense, and of the best quality; but it had no other effect upon Dora than to depress her spirits, and make her always nervous with the dread that it would be her turn next.
